verses.text: Around that time, King Herod began arresting some people from the church to mistreat them.
He had James, John’s brother, killed with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he also arrested Peter. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting him, Herod put him in prison and assigned four squads of four soldiers each to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out for the people after Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, while the church prayed earnestly to God for him.
The night before Herod was to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, chained with two chains. Guards stood watch at the prison entrance.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood beside him, and a light shone in the cell. The angel tapped Peter on the side to wake him and said, “Quick, get up!” The chains fell from Peter’s hands.
The angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did. Then the angel said, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”
Peter followed him out, but he didn’t realize that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guard posts and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them by itself. They went outside and walked down one street, then the angel suddenly left him.
When Peter came to his senses, he said, “Now I know for sure the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod and from everything the Jewish people expected to happen.”
After thinking it over, he went to the home of Mary, the mother of John also called Mark. Many people were gathered there, praying.
Peter knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
She recognized Peter’s voice and was so excited that she forgot to open the gate. She ran inside and announced that Peter was standing outside.
They said to her, “You’re out of your mind!” But she kept insisting it was true. They said, “It must be his angel.”
Meanwhile Peter kept knocking. When they opened the gate and saw him, they were stunned.

He motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. “Tell James and the other brothers and sisters,” he said. Then he left and went somewhere else.
When morning came, the soldiers were in an uproar, wondering what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched for him and couldn’t find him. He questioned the guards and ordered them executed. Then he left Judea and went down to Caesarea, where he stayed.

Herod was furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came together to meet with him. After winning over Blastus, the king’s personal aide, they asked for peace because their region depended on the king’s territory for its food supply.
On the appointed day, Herod put on his royal clothes, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.
The crowd shouted, “That’s the voice of a god, not a human!”
At once an angel of the Lord struck Herod because he didn’t give God the glory. Worms consumed him, and he died.
But God’s word kept spreading and growing.
After completing their work, Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, bringing John, also called Mark, with them.
